content: Your doctor has prescribed cefazolin, an antibiotic, to treat your infection. This medication will be administered either by injection into a large muscle, such as your buttock or hip, or through an intravenous (IV) fluid that will drip into your vein via a needle or catheter over a 30-minute period, two to four times a day. Cefazolin works by eliminating bacteria responsible for various infections, including those affecting the lungs, skin, bones, joints, stomach, blood, heart valves, and urinary tract. In some cases, cefazolin may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness of the treatment and check for side effects using laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your infection and symptoms respond to the medication. Precautions Before Using Cefazolin: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to cefazolin, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, probenecid (Benemid), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney, liver, or gastrointestinal diseases, particularly colitis. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking cefazolin, contact your doctor immediately. If you have diabetes and regularly check your urine for sugar, use Clinistix or TesTape. Avoid using Clinitest tablets, as cefazolin may cause false-positive results. Administering Cefazolin: Before administering cefazolin, inspect the solution carefully. It should be clear and free of floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or examine the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider's instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not stop your treatment prematurely, as this could worsen your infection and potentially lead to hospitalization. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. If you encounter a mechanical problem, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, stop the infusion and contact your healthcare provider immediately to ensure your therapy continues without interruption. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Cefazolin may cause some side effects. If the medication is injected into a muscle, it may be mixed with lidocaine (Xylocaine) to reduce pain at the injection site. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Diarrhea Stomach pain Upset stomach Vomiting Severe Side Effects: Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Skin rash Itching Hives Unusual bleeding or bruising Difficulty breathing Sore mouth or throat If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Cefazolin: If you are receiving cefazolin intravenously, you will likely be instructed to store it in the refrigerator or freezer. Take your next dose out of the refrigerator one hour before use and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If you are told to store additional cefazolin in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator for the next day’s use. Do not refreeze the medication. If you are receiving cefazolin intramuscularly, your healthcare provider will provide specific storage instructions. Always store the medication as directed and ensure you understand the proper storage requirements. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will instruct you on how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If you suspect an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving cefazolin intravenously or subcutaneously, be aware of the symptoms of a catheter-related infection, which occurs at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
